subject: Culture
title: Death and Children
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Death and Children.

hook.text: In Mexico, children eat candy skulls on Día de los Muertos. Death is a sweet visitor, not a monster.

buildup.text: Western cultures shield children from death. Mexican, Balinese, and Ghanaian cultures include them in rituals.

discovery.text: Psychologists find that children who attend funerals process grief better than those excluded from them.

twist.text: Disney kills more parents on screen than any other studio. We expose kids to fictional death but hide real death.

climax.text: Cultures that include children in death rituals produce adults with lower death anxiety scores.

punchline.text: Protecting kids from death teaches them to fear it.

quiz.question: What do Mexican children eat during Día de los Muertos?
